title: Ionic and covalent bonding, Lewis structures
objective: Recognize bonding models and draw atoms, molecules and polyatomic ions with correct electron counts.

blocks.title: Lewis structure
blocks.caption: Two C=O bonds and two lone pairs on each oxygen give the full 16-electron budget.

blocks.title: Common errors
blocks.md: Count the charge before drawing. A multiple bond reuses a lone pair. Hydrogen gets two electrons and is terminal. One structure does not show three-dimensional geometry by itself.

blocks.title: Exam practice
blocks.md: Count every electron pair in a proposed drawing before deciding whether a formal-charge or geometric choice makes sense.

blocks.title: Lewis symbols for ionic compounds
blocks.focus: Compare the electron counts before and after ions form.

blocks.title: A molecule with two multiple bonds
blocks.answer: $\ce{O=C=O}$ with two lone pairs on each O.

steps.title: Count and connect
steps.why: Carbon is the central atom and oxygen is terminal.

steps.title: Improve both sides
steps.md: After placing terminal lone pairs, convert one pair on each O into another bond.
steps.why: Two double bonds complete the carbon octet and give zero formal charges.

blocks.title: A polyatomic cation
blocks.answer: Four N–H single bonds and no N lone pair.

steps.title: Use the budget
steps.md: Place all eight electrons in the four single bonds.
steps.why: N has an octet, each H a duet, and N carries formal charge +1.
